title: Files, folders & cloud sync
blurb: OneDrive, iCloud, Dropbox, lost or deleted files, search, file types.

remedies.title: I saved a file but can't find it
remedies.why: Apps save to their last-used folder, often Documents, Downloads or OneDrive.

steps.text: Search by name from the taskbar or File Explorer's search box; File Explorer › Home shows Recent files.
Spotlight (⌘Space) by name; Finder › Recents.
In the app, File › Open › Recent shows where it went.
Check Downloads, Documents, Desktop and OneDrive/iCloud.

remedies.title: Show file extensions (.pdf, .docx) and hidden files
remedies.why: Extensions are hidden by default, which hides the real file type.

steps.text: File Explorer › View › Show › File name extensions and Hidden items.
Finder › Settings › Advanced › Show all filename extensions; ⌘+Shift+. shows hidden files.

remedies.title: Dropbox or Google Drive isn't syncing
remedies.why: Sync is paused, signed out, out of storage, or a file can't be uploaded.

steps.text: Open its icon in the taskbar/menu bar: resume, and read the error.
Check storage left in the account.
Quit and reopen the app; sign out and in if needed.
On a Mac, allow it in Login Items & Extensions › File Providers.

remedies.title: Sync a SharePoint or Teams folder to my computer
remedies.why: OneDrive can show SharePoint/Teams libraries in File Explorer or Finder.

steps.text: In SharePoint or Teams › Files, choose "Add shortcut to My files" (preferred) or Sync.
The folder appears under OneDrive in File Explorer / Finder.
Remove it later from OneDrive settings › Account, or delete the shortcut.

remedies.title: Can't delete, move or rename a file: "in use"
symptoms: the action can't be completed because the file is open
remedies.why: An app (sometimes the preview pane, antivirus or sync) still has the file open.

steps.text: Close apps that might have it open, and close File Explorer's preview pane.
Resource Monitor › CPU › Associated Handles: search the file name to see which app holds it.
Pause OneDrive/Dropbox for a moment.
Restart if nothing else works.

remedies.title: Copying files is very slow
remedies.why: Many tiny files, a slow USB stick or port, or copying over Wi-Fi.

steps.text: Zip many small files into one first.
Use a USB 3 port (often blue or marked SS) and a USB 3 drive.
Copy over a cable rather than Wi-Fi for large network copies.
Pause sync and antivirus scans during big copies.

remedies.title: PDF won't open, prints wrong, or asks for a password
remedies.why: The PDF is protected, damaged, or uses features the viewer doesn't support.

steps.text: Open it in another viewer: a browser, Preview (Mac), Adobe Reader, or DeskFolio.
Password-protected PDFs need the password from the sender.
Forms work best in Adobe Reader or DeskFolio; some browsers can't save filled forms.

remedies.title: Get an older version of a file
remedies.why: OneDrive, SharePoint, iCloud, Time Machine and File History keep older versions.

steps.text: OneDrive/SharePoint: right-click the file › Version history.
File History: right-click › Restore previous versions.
In Pages/Numbers/Keynote/Preview: File › Revert To › Browse All Versions; or Time Machine.
